r3_travel_c1.5: Mine's tiny. I can squeeze it in next to yours.
r3_travel_c1.6: Please don't touch it. It has a cake inside.
r3_travel_c1.7: A cake? For a five-hour flight?
r3_travel_c1.8: It's my sister's wedding cake. Top layer only.
r3_travel_c1.9: Is everything okay here? That bag is actually mine.

r3_work_c1.1: Okay, last item. Any thoughts on the new schedule?
r3_work_c1.10: I'm so sorry. That was very unprofessional.
r3_work_c1.11: That being said, it's the most honest thing anyone said today.
r3_work_c1.12: The client says they're asleep at eight too.
r3_work_c1.14: Nine-thirty. All because of you and the cat.
r3_work_c1.2: Sorry, give me a second. My cat's on the keyboard.
r3_work_c1.3: Take your time. We love the cat.
r3_work_c1.4: Okay. To be honest, the Monday meeting feels a little early.
r3_work_c1.5: Fair. How early is too early?
r3_work_c1.6: Eight is fine. Seven means I'm still asleep. Actually, I'm still asleep at eight.
r3_work_c1.7: You know you're not muted, right?
r3_work_c1.8: Oh no. My bad. Everyone heard that?

r4_work_d1.1: Do you have a minute? There's something I've been meaning to bring up.
r4_work_d1.10: Which company, if you don't mind me asking?
r4_work_d1.11: The design studio by the bridge. Why are you smiling?
r4_work_d1.12: Because they called me too. They want a team lead. And, apparently, a team.
r4_work_d1.13: Wait. So they're trying to hire both of us?
r4_work_d1.14: Looks like it. So now we have two offers and one very nervous boss upstairs.
r4_work_d1.16: It's up to you. But I already booked the big meeting room for Friday.
r4_work_d1.2: Sure. Close the door if it's the kind of thing that needs a closed door.
r4_work_d1.3: I got an offer from another company last week. A pretty good one.
r4_work_d1.4: I had a feeling. You've been wearing a nice shirt on Tuesdays.
r4_work_d1.5: To be honest, I'd rather stay. I like this team and what we're building.
r4_work_d1.6: That's good to hear. What would it take to keep you?
r4_work_d1.7: A raise that's closer to their number, and one remote day a week.
r4_work_d1.8: That's a reasonable ask. I can't promise their number, but I can fight for it.
r4_work_d1.9: That being said, I need an answer by Friday. They want me to start soon.

t1_office_g1.1: Hi Grace. Could you confirm whether my vacation request has been approved?
t1_office_g1.2: I'm not sure. The new HR system was updated over the weekend.
t1_office_g1.3: You're not sure? Approvals are handled by your department.
t1_office_g1.4: I know that I approved several requests this morning.
t1_office_g1.6: Then the system asked if I wanted to clear all pending requests.
t1_office_g1.7: And you clicked "yes" without reading it.
t1_office_g1.8: No worries. Nobody in this building is going anywhere this year.

t1_office_g10.1: I forwarded the compensation file to the team. I felt confident about it.
t1_office_g10.3: I assumed it was a typo for "confident."
t1_office_g10.4: Oh no. Did you send it to "Marketing Team" or "All Staff"?
t1_office_g10.5: All Staff. Every branch. The reach was considerable.
t1_office_g10.6: Everyone now knows Raj earns more than his supervisor.
t1_office_g10.7: You're kidding. That's the actual emergency here.
t1_office_g10.8: I'll be considerate and recall the message. From my inbox, at least.

t1_office_g11.1: We came to finalize the service agreement this afternoon.
t1_office_g11.2: Excellent. Would you prefer a pen or the tablet?
t1_office_g11.3: To be honest, our legal team decided to postpone the signing.
t1_office_g11.4: You came here to sign, in order to postpone?
t1_office_g11.5: There's still plenty of time to review the terms.
t1_office_g11.6: There's also a sandwich to finish. In your left hand.
t1_office_g11.7: I came to have lunch with my favorite vendor. The contract was a bonus.
t1_office_g11.8: Sounds good. Lunch is forty dollars per person. Sign here.

t1_office_g12.1: Would you mind staying late to review the vendor contracts?
t1_office_g12.2: Not really. I enjoy leaving the office on time.
t1_office_g12.3: You can't avoid working overtime during the audit season.
t1_office_g12.4: I've finished trying. It's been a long quarter.
t1_office_g12.5: Thank you for being so transparent about your priorities.
t1_office_g12.6: No problem. I left the building without saving the contract file, though.
t1_office_g12.7: You considered ending your career before the audit?
t1_office_g12.8: I'm staying. And enjoying it. Very much.

t1_office_g13.1: Honestly, how did my presentation go?
t1_office_g13.2: The entire audience looked bored by slide three.
t1_office_g13.4: The slides were boring. You, however, were interesting.
t1_office_g13.6: You presented last year's figures. From a different department. Very exciting.
t1_office_g13.7: I mean, the client seemed genuinely excited.
t1_office_g13.8: He was excited to leave early.

t1_office_g14.1: The label reads "shipped items — this side of the dock."
t1_office_g14.3: So the damaged printer returned by the client goes…
t1_office_g14.4: With the shipped items. It's clearly not personnel.
t1_office_g14.5: Hold on. Who is the person handling returns this week?
t1_office_g14.6: The gentleman standing next to the delivery truck.
t1_office_g14.7: Oh no. That truck just left. With the printer. And Tom's new laptop.
t1_office_g14.8: A shipped laptop. Please call Tom before he notices.

t1_office_g15.1: Let's discuss about the revised delivery schedule.
t1_office_g15.2: Discuss the schedule, Tom. No "about" needed.
t1_office_g15.3: Noted. I'll attend the meeting in person tomorrow.
t1_office_g15.4: Please arrive at the conference room by nine.
t1_office_g15.5: I always respond to meeting invitations promptly.
t1_office_g15.6: You responded to the last one three weeks after the meeting.
t1_office_g15.7: Just kidding. I'll contact you as soon as I arrive.
t1_office_g15.8: Of course. Contact me, not "contact to me."

t1_office_g16.1: Who distributed the compensation file to the entire company?
t1_office_g16.4: The attachment was selected. The send button was pressed.
t1_office_g16.5: I mean, buttons don't press themselves in this building.
t1_office_g16.7: "Was happened" is not English. Try again.
t1_office_g16.8: Fair enough. The incident happened. By me.

t1_office_g17.1: Our accounting team has waited for the invoice since Monday.
t1_office_g17.2: I sent it on Monday morning, with the tracking number.
t1_office_g17.3: We haven't received anything for a full week.
t1_office_g17.4: Just to confirm, which address should it have gone to?
t1_office_g17.5: The one I have used for ten years. Everyone has it.
t1_office_g17.6: You changed it last month and notified us yourself.
t1_office_g17.7: My bad. I have just located it. In the spam folder.
t1_office_g17.8: So your team has waited for nothing since Monday.

t1_office_g18.1: This model is considerably cheaper than the one we use now.
t1_office_g18.2: That one is more comfortable than anything in this catalog.
t1_office_g18.3: Procurement policy says we purchase the cheapest option available.
t1_office_g18.4: The cheapest option is as hard as a concrete block.
t1_office_g18.5: Concrete is free. Order twenty units for the whole floor.
t1_office_g18.6: Never have I seen an invoice this large for office chairs.
t1_office_g18.7: Twenty chairs plus freight. Shipping turned out to be the most expensive line item.
t1_office_g18.8: No way. Told you — the cheapest option is always the costliest.

t1_office_g2.1: You missed the first twenty minutes of the client meeting. Reason?
t1_office_g2.2: I was late because of heavy traffic downtown.
t1_office_g2.3: Although you live two floors above this office.
t1_office_g2.4: The elevator was out of service because maintenance was scheduled today.
t1_office_g2.5: Despite the staircase right next to it?
t1_office_g2.6: Honestly, I took the stairs. In the wrong direction.
t1_office_g2.7: Are you kidding me? The client asked if you still work here.
t1_office_g2.8: I'll arrive early tomorrow, because I'm sleeping under my desk.

t1_office_g3.1: Lunch poll results. Either we order pizza or we skip lunch entirely.
t1_office_g3.2: That's not a poll. That's a hostage situation.
t1_office_g3.3: Pizza is not only affordable but also delivered within thirty minutes.
t1_office_g3.4: Fine. One large pizza for the team. For real, just one.
t1_office_g3.5: Both the regional manager and the client requested their own.
t1_office_g3.7: Three. Neither the manager nor the client wanted to share.
t1_office_g3.8: No way. Then the third one goes on your expense report.

t1_office_g4.1: Someone removed the yogurt which was clearly labeled with my name.
t1_office_g4.2: The employee who took it left the spoon in the sink.
t1_office_g4.3: A spoon whose handle is company blue. That narrows it down.
t1_office_g4.4: To everyone on this floor, including the cleaning staff.
t1_office_g4.5: What I need is a name, not a suspect list.
t1_office_g4.6: Hold on. Someone is wiping her mouth near the copier.
t1_office_g4.7: It expired yesterday. Consider it a safety inspection.
t1_office_g4.8: I knew it. You owe me a yogurt which hasn't expired.

t1_office_g5.1: I need the revised proposal by Friday. The board meets on Monday.
t1_office_g5.2: Just to confirm, by Friday or until Friday?
t1_office_g5.4: By means I deliver it. Until means I keep suffering.
t1_office_g5.5: Then by Friday. And please complete the budget section within three business days.
t1_office_g5.6: Got it. Today is Thursday, Tom.
t1_office_g5.7: Oh. Then in one day, I suppose.
t1_office_g5.8: So I'll be suffering until Friday after all.

t1_office_g6.1: Quarterly sales increased by thirty percent. I'd like to discuss a raise.
t1_office_g6.2: However, the budget for salary adjustments was cut by forty.
t1_office_g6.3: In addition, I've covered weekend shifts for three months.
t1_office_g6.4: Therefore, you have no personal life. That's not a budget issue.
t1_office_g6.5: Otherwise, I'll accept the offer from the company across the street.
t1_office_g6.6: The company across the street is a bakery.
t1_office_g6.7: Fair enough. That's it, I'm submitting my resignation.
t1_office_g6.8: Sit down. Coffee. Your adjustment is effective in January. Tell no one.

t1_office_g7.1: This copier is out of order again.
t1_office_g7.2: Use the other one by the window. It was serviced last week.
t1_office_g7.3: The other one is displaying an error code too.
t1_office_g7.4: Then try another one on the third floor.
t1_office_g7.5: Not again. That one jams every time I print double-sided.
t1_office_g7.6: Fine. The others are in the basement storage room.
t1_office_g7.7: Come on. Why are all of them out of service at once?
t1_office_g7.8: Olivia printed the annual budget. All 400 pages. In color. Twice.

t1_office_g8.1: I placed an order for three equipments for the new branch.
t1_office_g8.2: Equipment doesn't take a plural. Neither does your overtime pay.
t1_office_g8.3: Then what exactly did the supplier ship?
t1_office_g8.4: Three of every item on the list, according to the delivery confirmation.
t1_office_g8.5: My bad. I also requested "furnitures" on the same form.
t1_office_g8.6: Seriously? That explains the three coffee machines in the hallway.
t1_office_g8.7: Some advice beforehand would have been appreciated.
t1_office_g8.8: Advice is uncountable. So is the damage to your reputation.

t1_office_g9.1: The quarterly report. Still not submitted?
t1_office_g9.3: Almost is not a time. The deadline was an hour ago.
t1_office_g9.4: I've already finalized the title page and the table of contents.
t1_office_g9.6: Not yet. But I hardly slept this week.
t1_office_g9.7: You hardly slept because you were hardly working?
t1_office_g9.8: I swear the analysis is coming right now. Just the analysis.
